content.title: Every EGOT Winner and What They Won For
content.text: See a full list of the entertainment luminaries who became EGOT winners by snagging an Emmy, a Grammy, an Oscar, and a Tony—sometimes more than one of each.Clockwise: Mel Brooks at the 1998 Emmy Awards; John Legend at the 2006 Grammy Awards; Whoopi Goldberg at the 1991 Oscars; Andrew Lloyd Webber at the 2018 Tony Awards; Barbra Streisand at the 1987 Grammy Awards; Audrey Hepburn at the 1968 Tony Awards.All from Getty Images.What is an EGOT? Technically, it’s the term for someone who has won an Emmy, a Grammy, an Oscar, and a Tony. But more significantly, the acronym signifies an entertainer who has dominated all forms of entertainment, from stage and screen to music and television. It’s a major achievement to win even one of these prizes, but to win all of the top prizes in entertainment is to join an upper echelon of legends. Why settle for “Look Mom, I won a [insert one top prize of your choice here]!” when you can overachieve your way to a full trophy closet, and a place in the history books?How many EGOT winners are there? There are 21 EGOT winners—27 if you include EGOTs with noncompetitive awards, such as lifetime achievement honors—including two winners who have EGOT-ed twice. Here is the list of every EGOT winner, in the order in which they EGOT-ed.Richard Rogers – May 22, 1962The first ever EGOT winner was none other than half of the composing team that gave us such timeless musicals as The Sound of Music and South Pacific, which respectively earned him his first Grammy (best show album—original cast) and Tony (best musical and best score). His and Oscar Hammerstein II’s State Fair song “It Might as Well Be Spring” earned the best-song Academy Award. But Hammerstein himself never earned EGOT status: Rogers earned his Emmy after Hammerstein’s death, for outstanding achievement in original music composed for television for Winston Churchill: The Valiant Years.Barbra Streisand (noncompetitive) – April 19, 1970In 1964, Barbra Streisand was the second woman to win the album-of-the-year Grammy (after Judy Garland) for her debut recording, The Barbra Streisand Album. The next year, she won her first of five career Emmys for her special My Name is Barbra. For her indelible performance as Fanny Brice in Funny Girl, Streisand would be the only ever best-actress Oscar to win in a tie, sharing the award with Katharine Hepburn for The Lion in Winter. Though she did not win a Tony for creating the same role on Broadway, the Tony Awards gave Streisand a special ”Star of the Decade” prize in 1970. While some awards obsessives don’t consider noncompetitive awards eligible for EGOT status, who are we to take anything away from the incomparable Streisand–particularly when she was one of the quickest to earn EGOT status, achieving it within the span of six years?Helen Hayes – February 19, 1977After decades on stage and screen, Helen Hayes earned her EGOT status in 1977 with a spoken word Grammy for reading the Bill of Rights on Great American Documents. Hayes is also one of the few EGOTs who boasts winning each trophy in a different decade: She got her first Oscar in 1932 (for The Sin of Madelon Claudet, best actress); her first Tony in 1947 (for Happy Birthday, best actress in a play); and an Emmy in 1953 (for Schlitz Playhouse of Stars, best actress).Rita Moreno at the 1962 Oscars, with West Side Story co-star George Chakiris.Getty Images.Rita Moreno – September 11, 1977The same year Hayes achieved EGOT status, the Emmys clinched Rita Moreno’s EGOT when she won for a guest appearance on The Muppet Show, an episode in which she performs “Fever” with Animal. Moreno won her best-supporting-actress Oscar as Anita in West Side Story, and her Grammy for best recording for children with The Electric Company. She won her Tony for best-featured actress in a play for The Ritz. After taking the podium, Moreno told the Tony audience—dipping into character as her larger-than-life bathhouse performer character Googie Gomez—“The only thing I support in that show is my bits!” She’s continued to be one of the most decorated entertainers alive, with further accolades, including Kennedy Center Honors and a Peabody Award.Liza Minelli at the 1973 Oscars, with her father Vincente Minnelli.Getty Images.Liza Minnelli (noncompetitive) – February 21, 1990Liza Minnelli was the first person to begin their EGOT journey with a Tony Award (best lead actress in a musical, Flora the Red Menace). In 1973, she won back-to-back at the Oscars and Emmys for Cabaret and Liza with a Z, respectively. Her Grammy came in 1990, with a Grammy Legend tribute award. She accepted the honor by performing a disco version of Stephen Sondheim’s “Losing My Mind” and said in her acceptance speech, “Mostly, I’d like to thank the people who buy the records because they made it all possible.”John Gielgud – August 25, 1991Sir John Gielgud was the first British EGOT winner, the first queer EGOT winner, and the only male EGOT to win an Academy Award for acting (best-supporting actor, Arthur). His 1980 spoken-word Grammy for Ages of Man—a collection of Shakespeare speeches—also earned him a special Tony when he performed it on the stage over two decades prior. Gielgud earned two competitive acting Tonys as well: a foreign company award for The Importance of Being Earnest in 1948, and best director of a drama for Big Fish, Little Fish in 1961. Gielgud became the oldest person to cross the EGOT finish line when he won his Emmy for miniseries Summer’s Lease at the age of 87.Audrey Hepburn – March 1, 1994“It’s too much,” Audrey Hepburn sheepishly said upon receiving her Oscar for Roman Holiday in 1954. But the awards wouldn’t stop regardless of her modesty: She won a Tony for Ondine three days later. Hepburn remained beloved through her final days, becoming the first and only posthumous EGOT winner. Both her Emmy (informational programming, Gardens of the World With Audrey Hepburn) and Grammy (spoken-word album for children, Audrey Hepburn’s Enchanted Tales) were awarded following her death.Marvin Hamlisch – September 9, 1995Were it not for those pesky Emmys, Marvin Hamlisch would have had a meteoric rise to EGOT status. At the Academy Awards in 1974, he took home three Oscars—one of only 14 people to earn so many in one ceremony—for music from The Way We Were and The Sting. At the next Grammys, he earned four awards, including best new artist (one of only two people on this list to win that award). In 1976, he won the Tony for his original score to Broadway juggernaut A Chorus Line. But his EGOT wasn’t earned until 1995, when Hamlish got two Emmys for his work on Barbra: The Concert, the HBO broadcast of Barbra Streisand’s first concerts in decades.Jonathan Tunick – June 1, 1997If you think you have to be a household name to dominate the most coveted awards, think again! Jonathan Tunick earned his EGOT for a decades-spanning career as an orchestrator, music director, and composer, crossing the EGOT finish line in 1997 by winning a best-orchestrations Tony for the musical Titanic. Previously, he earned a 1978 Oscar for score adaptation (a now defunct category) for A Little Night Music. His Emmy arrived in 1982, for music directing Night of 100 Stars, and his Grammy in 1989, for his instrumental arrangement of Cleo Laine’s version of “No One is Alone.” He recently won his second orchestrations Tony for the revival of Merrily We Roll Along.Mel Brooks – June 3, 2001Mel Brooks is one of the few to begin their EGOT with an Emmy, earning a writing win for a variety show in 1967. His Oscar came for the original screenplay of The Producers, making Brooks the only person on this list to win an Oscar for screenwriting. A guest-starring run on Mad About You kicked off a late-career awards run, starting in 1997. Brooks won three consecutive Emmys for the series, a comedy album Grammy in 1999, and a trio of 2001 Tonys for the stage adaptation of The Producers. With his 2023 honorary Oscar, Brooks became only the second person to win a double EGOT, with at least two wins for each of the awards.Mike Nichols – November 4, 2001Though Mike Nichols won his Grammy for comedy performance alongside Elaine May in 1962, he is the only person among the EGOT winners to have been awarded for directing—he got an Oscar for The Graduate, and his first of nine Tonys for directing Barefoot in the Park. In 2001, he earned his EGOT status with multiple Emmys for HBO’s Wit. At Nichols’s AFI Lifetime Achievement in 2010, presenter Julia Roberts remarked on his EGOT status—at a time when there were less than half of the EGOT winners there are today.Whoopi Goldberg – June 2, 2002Like Nichols and Brooks, Whoopi Goldberg earned the “G” in her EGOT for a comedy recording, and hers was for the recording of her one-person Broadway show in 1986. After winning the best-supporting-actress Academy Award for her performance in Ghost and a special Emmy in 1997 for the Comic Relief benefit specials, her EGOT story was brought full circle with a Tony—not for reviving her solo act, but for producing the musical Thoroughly Modern Millie. Goldberg is the first Black EGOT winner.James Earl Jones (noncompetitive) – November 12, 2011James Earl Jones began his EGOT trajectory with a Tony for lead actor in The Great White Hope; he was nominated for an Oscar for recreating the role onscreen but didn’t win. Like Hayes, his Grammy came in the spoken-word category: Jones won for Great American Documents. (Surely there has never been another voice in human existence we would rather hear reading the Constitution than his.) In 1991, he won a lead-actor-in-a-drama Emmy for one-season-wonder Gabriel’s Fire, making him the only male performer on this list with an acting Emmy that wasn’t for a guest or miniseries role. Jones’s honorary Oscar in 2011 made him the first person to complete their EGOT with an Oscar.Scott Rudin – February 12, 2012Even the industry’s most notorious figures can achieve a spot in the Hall of Fame of entertainment, like producer Scott Rudin—who first earned an Emmy for the children’s program He Makes Me Feel Like Dancin’. He became an EGOT thanks to the Grammy won by the cast recording for the Broadway musical The Book of Mormon, after a best picture Oscar win for No Country for Old Men and numerous Tony wins that began with a best-musical victory in 1994 for Passion. After Rudin’s history of alleged physical and verbal abuse was exposed in 2021, and the Broadway community called for Rudin to exit his producing duties for ongoing and incoming productions, he released a statement saying, “After a period of reflection, I’ve made the decision to step back from active participation on our Broadway productions, effective immediately.”Robert Lopez – March 2, 2014While almost all EGOT winners have additional prize wins to their credit, composer Robert Lopez is the only double EGOT winner ever for entirely competitive categories—meaning he has won each of the EGOT prizes (at least) twice. He is also the only Asian and Filipino EGOT winner. His awards run began in 2004, when he won a Tony for his original score for Avenue Q. In 2008, he won a daytime Emmy for music composition for Wonder Pets, and in 2012, won a Grammy for best-musical-theater album for The Book of Mormon. With further songwriting accolades including Frozen, Coco, and “Agatha All Along,” Lopez earned his first EGOT when he got the best-original-song Oscar for “Let It Go” a week after his 39th birthday, which made him the youngest EGOT award winner ever.Harry Belafonte (noncompetitive) – November 8, 2014The legend and activist earned three-quarters of his EGOT in the span of a decade, starting with a Tony for distinguished performance in John Murray Anderson’s Almanac in 1954 (the same ceremony Audrey Hepburn was awarded), a variety-performance Emmy for The Revlon Revue in 1960, and a best-folk-performance Grammy in 1961 for his album Swing Dat Hammer. Like James Earl Jones, Belafonte joined the EGOT club with a tribute Oscar. In the moving acceptance speech for his Jean Hersholt Humanitarian Award, Belafonte mused about the potential for Hollywood to create societal change, saying, “Perhaps we as artists and as visionaries, for what’s better in the human heart and the human soul, could influence citizens everywhere in the world to see the better side of who and what we are as a species.”Quincy Jones at the 1982 Grammy Awards.Getty Images.Quincy Jones (noncompetitive) – June 12, 2016With almost 30 Grammy wins (including a Grammy Legend Award) and both honorary and humanitarian Oscars, Quincy Jones is perhaps the most awarded person on the list of EGOT winners—and one of only two EGOTs to win an album-of-the-year Grammy. His first Grammy was for instrumental arrangement in 1964 for “I Can’t Stop Loving You,” and his Emmy came in 1977 for composing the score for Roots. But he finally got his EGOT victory by winning a best musical revival Tony in 2016 as part of the producing team for The Color Purple revival that made a star out of Cynthia Erivo.Andrew Lloyd Webber – September 9, 2018Mega composer Andrew Lloyd Webber’s EGOT journey belongs largely to his 1980 Eva Peron musical Evita, which earned him his first Tony and Grammy awards ( for original score and cast album, respectively). In 1997, Webber co-wrote “You Must Love Me” for Alan Parker’s Madonna-led film adaptation of the show, earning an original song Academy Award. Webber also earned Tonys and Grammys for Cats—but unsurprisingly no Oscars for the musical’s reviled film adaptation. It was another musical entirely that led to Webber’s Emmy: Jesus Christ Superstar Live in Concert, which won the outstanding live variety special award in 2018. Of the potential to finally EGOT, Webber told Vanity Fair in 2018 “You know what? It’s great when you get awards, but I’m not sort of obsessed with the things.” But if you think that’s the last you hear of that staged concert, just hold tight…Tim Rice – September 9, 2018Lyricist and librettist Tim Rice nearly matches Webber’s EGOT record, including the Emmy win for Jesus Christ Superstar and the Tony and Grammy wins for Evita. But prior to their “You Must Love Me” Oscar, Rice won another Academy Award for original song along with Alan Menken for Aladdin’s “A Whole New World.” It was the first of three wins in the category for Rice in the 1990s. Rice’s wins include collaborations with three other EGOT winners, including Webber, Menken, and…John Legend – September 9, 2018Yes: the live Jesus Christ Superstar was responsible for pushing three people to an EGOT, including its multi-hyphenate producer-star, John Legend. Legend’s Grammy debut in 2006 earned him three statues, including best new artist and best R&B album (Get Lifted). The twenty-teens wrapped up the EGOT for Legend quickly: he earned an original song Oscar for Selma’s “Glory in 2015 and produced the revival of Jitney for a best revival of a play Tony in 2017. The morning after EGOTing, Legend’s wife Chrissy Teigen posted a video of him making what he called “EGOT pancakes.”Alan Menken – July 26, 2020Among the most awarded EGOT winners is composer Alan Menken, thanks largely to his songwriting duties for Disney in the 1990s. During that decade, Menken won 10 of his 11 Grammys, along with four original song and four original score Oscars, all beginning with The Little Mermaid. Starting with the 1996 ceremony, the Academy Awards split the original score category in two–dramatic and musical/comedy–due in part to Disney’s (and therefore largely Menken’s) dominance over it. In 1990, Menken earned a special Emmy for teaching kids to say no to drugs with his contributions to Cartoon All-Stars to the Rescue, but later won a daytime Emmy for original song for Rapunzel’s Tangled Adventure. But Menken would not achieve the EGOT until the Broadway production of Newsies arrived in 2012, earning Menken an original score Tony.Jennifer Hudson at the 2024 Tony Awards.Getty Images.Jennifer Hudson – June 12, 2022Jennifer Hudson’s success story from American Idol contestant to EGOT winner is the stuff of legend. After winning a supporting actress Oscar for her towering performance as Effie White in Dreamgirls, she would win the best R&B album Grammy for her self-titled debut and an interactive media Daytime Emmy for Baba Yaga. But when she won the best musical Tony as part of A Strange Loop’s producing team, she was unaware of the greater thing she’d just achieved—telling Gayle King she didn’t realize it until hearing crowd chants of “EGOT! EGOT!” Hudson also posted a photo with all of her EGOT hardware.Viola Davis at the 2023 Grammy Awards.Getty Images.Viola Davis – February 5, 2023“I just EGOT!” Viola Davis cheered when accepting her Grammy for the audiobook of her memoir Finding Me, delivering maybe the first acceptance speech to acknowledge the achievement in the moment. When she earned a lead actress in a drama Emmy for the first season of How to Get Away with Murder, she became the first Black actress to win in that category; along with James Earl Jones, she is also the only acting EGOT to win an Emmy for playing a recurring character. Davis earned both her Tony and her Oscar for playing the role of Rose Maxson in August Wilson’s Fences.Frank Marshall (noncompetitive) – May 22, 2023Did you know that such a thing as a Sports Emmy exists?! Well, they do—and they’re what helped net producer/director Frank Marshall his EGOT, when he won outstanding long documentary at the Sports Emmys for The Redeem Team. He is the fastest person to achieve EGOT status, earning all four prizes in just four years. His run started in 2019, when he received an honorary Oscar–making him the only EGOT who started their EGOT journey with an honorary prize. He won his Grammy for best music film for Jazz Fest: A New Orleans Story, and he earned his Tony as part of A Strange Loop’s producing team.Elton John – January 15, 2024Sir Elton John’s mantle is adorned with far fewer Grammys than you might expect: the legend never even won one until collaborating with Dionne Warwick for their 1987 version of “That’s What Friends Are For.” Collaborating with Tim Rice brought the next two letters of his EGOT, with an original song Oscar for “Can You Feel the Love Tonight” and an original score Tony for Aida. Though surgery kept the rocket man from attending the Emmys where his EGOT was cemented (he won the live variety special Emmy for the broadcast of his North American farewell at Dodger Stadium), producer Ben Winston capped his acceptance speech by honoring Elton’s new EGOT status.Benj Pasek and Justin Paul – September 8, 2024The songwriting twosome are the only EGOT winners with an entirely shared track record, achieving Tony and Grammy with Dear Evan Hansen and an Oscar for La La Land’s “City of Stars.” Though they defeated Robert Lopez’s record for fastest to an EGOT, Pasek was roughly one month too old to overtake Lopez’s record for youngest person to EGOT. In the press room after their EGOT-sealing Emmy win for an original song for an Only Murders in the Building tune co-written with Marc Shaiman and Scott Wittman, Paul said, “I think that [writing the song] alongside two of our musical heroes, who gave us our very first job in television, is what makes it most meaningful.”Steven Spielberg – February 1, 2026The filmmaking icon isThe Story of Charvet (Or, How to Keep Luxury Quiet)“You’ll Answer in Hell”: The Families of Some ICE Agents Are Speaking Out“You’ll Answer in Hell”: The Families of Some ICE Agents Are Speaking OutChris Feil is a freelance film journalist located in Columbus, OH.
